title: Air pollution from electricity for AI data centres
one_line: Power plants and backup generators that supply AI data centres emit fine particles and ozone precursors, which cause premature deaths downwind.
scope_note: Contiguous United States only. The three health studies cover all data centres; the AI share is attributed by the model.

assumptions.description: DALYs lost per premature death attributable to data-centre air pollution in the US.
assumptions.rationale: PLACEHOLDER: no source read yet. Air-pollution deaths in the US fall mostly on older adults with cardiovascular and respiratory disease, so years of life lost per death are well below the global average; the range is a wide guess spanning that. Morbidity (years lived with disability, e.g. asthma) is assumed small next to years of life lost.
assumptions.replace_with: GBD 2023 (IHME): ratio of US DALYs to deaths attributable to ambient PM2.5 and ozone, by year.

assumptions.description: Deaths per TWh in 2027–2031 relative to the study year (grid change).
assumptions.rationale: Han et al.'s own 2028 projections imply ~11% fewer deaths per TWh than in 2023 (Table 1: 705/325 and 1262/580 vs 433/176.39), and the grid is expected to get cleaner; but data-centre demand is delaying coal retirements in some regions (Han et al., p. 2). Range: up to 30% cleaner by 2031, or no change.
assumptions.replace_with: A projection of US power-sector air-pollution mortality per TWh to 2031 (e.g. EPA or EIA scenarios run through a health model).

assumptions.description: Growth of US data-centre electricity after 2028, as a fraction of the 2023–2028 scenario growth rate.
assumptions.rationale: No source read projects US data-centre electricity beyond 2028. Assumes growth continues but does not accelerate; grid-connection and chip-supply constraints make slower growth plausible.
assumptions.replace_with: A US data-centre electricity projection to 2030 or later (e.g. EPRI, IEA, or a later LBNL report).

assumptions.description: Annual growth of non-AI data-centre electricity after 2023.
assumptions.rationale: LBNL: conventional server electricity doubled from about 30 to nearly 60 TWh over 2014–2023, about 8% a year. Assumes non-AI demand grows no faster than that, and possibly not at all.
assumptions.replace_with: LBNL's 2028 breakdown by server type (Figure 5.1 data) or a later report.

limitations: US only; no source read yet gives a global estimate.
None of the three health studies is AI-specific; AI's share of data-centre electricity is attributed in the model, from two estimates that disagree.
The conversion from deaths to DALYs is a placeholder assumption until a GBD-derived source is added.
No source projects US data-centre electricity beyond 2028; 2029–2031 extrapolates under an assumption.
The GEOS-Chem interval covers concentration-response uncertainty only.

changelog.why: Finishes the work interrupted on 2026-11-25. The air-pollution model now declares its fixed inputs (2023 electricity, AI-share estimates) as parameters instead of hidden constants, so `aiwelfare model` and the card show every number used.

changelog.change: Milestone 1 (part 1): schemas, CLI scaffold, data-centre air-pollution sources and claims
changelog.why: Records decisions D11-D15 (approved by the maintainer) and the source-integration procedure. Air pollution is the first card built from real evidence: three independent models of deaths from US data-centre electricity (Han et al. v4, Chen et al. 2026, Muller 2026) plus LBNL's electricity scenarios. 28 claims, each quote checked verbatim against its PDF. Work in progress: model and card are not finished.
